title: When the Locker Breaks
premise: Bram Eriksen, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, discovers that his late grandmother's recipe box contains coded instructions to a hidden network of students who have been quietly protecting scholarship kids from the academy's exploitative 'Patronage' system. When the box is exposed, Bram and his ragtag found family — rival Deb, groundskeeper's son Theo, and cryptic librarian Ms. Okafor — are blackmailed into competing in the prestigious Vantage Games, a championship the school uses as cover for its real contest: deciding which students' futures get funded and which get erased. To survive, they must win both the public games and the secret one beneath them, exposing the Patronage before the final bell. In the end, Bram sacrifices his own scholarship to break the system, and the family he found — not the academy — carries him forward.
about_author: Wendell Marchetti is a former boarding-school kitchen worker who spent six years collecting the whispered stories of scholarship kids before writing them into fiction. He lives near a lake, bakes bread badly, and insists every recipe he publishes contains at least one lie.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Establishes Hollowmere Academy's glittering surface and Bram's precarious scholarship: tutoring rich kids, eating last in the dining hall, lying to his mom that it's all fine. Emotional beat: brittle denial, the ache of being grateful for a place that doesn't want him.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sorting his grandmother's belongings, Bram finds the tin recipe box — but cards like 'Grief Casserole' contain maps, names, and dates instead of ingredients. The last card is addressed, impossibly, to him. Beat: grief curdling into wonder and dread.

chapters.title: Deb Kowalczyk Hates Him Slightly Less
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He decodes a card pointing to the old greenhouse and walks straight into rival Deb mid-heist of seed ledgers. Mutual blackmail becomes uneasy alliance when they realize their grandmothers were in the same network. Beat: rivalry cracking into recognition.

chapters.title: What the Patronage Pays For
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Groundskeeper's son Theo shows them the ledger room where 'sponsorships' are actually debts — tuition traded for servitude or expulsion. His father was erased from records after asking questions. Beat: the horror under the polish, first taste of real stakes.

chapters.title: Ms. Okafor's Overdue Books
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The librarian reveals she was 'Card Seven' — the network's archivist — and that grandma's box is the master key the academy has hunted for decades. She agrees to help, reluctantly. Beat: an adult finally telling the truth; hope with a warning attached.

chapters.title: Vantage Season Opens
chapters.summary: Deb's POV. Headmaster Voss announces the Vantage Games, framing them as tradition and opportunity. Deb, hungry for the sailing title she's trained years for, resents being drafted into conspiracy. Beat: ambition versus conscience; the public game begins.

chapters.title: Trial by Obstacle
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. First event: a night orienteering race through campus. Bram and Deb deliberately place mid-pack while secretly photographing the route's restricted zones, which match a recipe card. Beat: competence and adrenaline; the two games overlap for the first time.

chapters.title: The Card That Burns
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A card self-destructs in Theo's hands — literal acid ink — and Voss's aide catches the smoke. Theo takes the blame alone rather than name the others. Beat: loyalty tested; guilt lands on Bram like a debt.

chapters.title: Visiting Hours
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Suspended pending inquiry, Theo is held on campus 'for his safety.' Bram visits through a service corridor and finds Theo surprisingly calm — he's been leaving chalk marks for other marked kids. Beat: found family solidifying; courage as quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Sailing on Borrowed Wind
chapters.summary: Deb's POV. The regatta: Deb must throw her heat to keep suspicion off the group, racing against everything she wants. She wins anyway, brilliantly, then lies about why. Beat: the cost of duty; love for the team outweighing the trophy she can't stop wanting.

chapters.title: Grandma's Last Instruction
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Decoding the final card requires a key Okafor refuses to give: it names the erasure list, including Bram. Grandma knew he'd be chosen. Beat: betrayal by the person who loved him most — protection that feels like abandonment.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Quiz-and-labyrinth team finals; the four win publicly while smuggling a copied ledger out inside a trophy case. Voss congratulates them warmly, which is worse than suspicion. Beat: triumph laced with dread; masks holding.

chapters.title: Okafor Breaks
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV (first departure). Pressured by Voss, who knows her history, she considers trading the box for her pension and her brother's debt. She burns one card instead — the wrong one. Beat: fear defeating principle; the plan hemorrhages.

chapters.title: What We Buried Under the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The group recovers the network's physical archive — decades of erased students' names — just ahead of Voss's men. Theo's father's file is there, still warm from someone else's search. Beat: grief made concrete; resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Voss privately offers Bram full funding, his mother's security, everything — if he surrenders the box and testifies the others acted alone. It's a genuinely good deal. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; love against duty made personal.

chapters.title: Deb's Confession
chapters.summary: Deb's POV. Deb admits she nearly took a similar deal weeks ago and tells the group before Voss can use it. Instead of fracturing, they re-plan around betrayal as a tactic: let her appear to flip. Beat: honesty as armor; trust rebuilt stronger for being tested.

chapters.title: The One That Does Matter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Beneath the Vantage finale, the real contest: a closed hearing where patrons vote the year's erasure list. The team infiltrates via the labyrinth's maintenance spine, guided by the burned card's surviving half. Beat: rising action cresting; no way back.

chapters.title: Final Bell
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax. Deb throws the public final on purpose to empty the stands; Theo floods the lower corridors' lights; Okafor walks in and identifies herself as Card Seven to stall the vote. Bram reaches the ledger table as Voss seals the doors. Beat: every thread converging at speed.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Cornered, Bram tears up his own scholarship contract on the record — making himself unownable — and reads the erased names aloud until the patrons' silence breaks. Voss falls not to exposure alone but to his own board's cowardice. Beat: sacrifice as victory; voice as weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Investigations begin; Okafor resigns rather than be rewarded, passing the archive to the students. Deb gets her reinstated title and gives the medal to Theo's father's memory wall. Beat: justice arriving imperfectly; grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Recipe for Four
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Summer's end: Bram, scholarshipless, plans state school and weekend shifts — and finds the group has quietly built him a fund from the network's old channels, now legal. Grandma's box gets a new first card, written by all four. Beat: warmth without sentimentality; the family holds.

chapters.title: When the Locker Breaks
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue. A new scholarship kid's locker jams; Bram helps her open it and slips a card inside — directions, not ingredients. The cycle continues, but this time on their terms. Beat: quiet hope; the story ends by beginning again.
